transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. As you all know, I recently received Grandma's stained-glass window — the 90-by-60-centimeter piece — and I want to see it properly displayed in the family home before our autumn gathering. We have three possible locations: the south-facing breakfast-room window, the west hallway, or the reading room. We also need to decide on a protective covering and lighting — either focused spotlights or a diffuse wall wash. And importantly, the window should remain available for family members to view without an appointment. Before I make any decisions, I'd like to do what I usually do: go around the table and hear what each of you knows, what you need, and what you can commit to regarding this project. So — who'd like to start?

transcript.text: I have something important to share on the protective covering. I spoke with conservator Dr. Lena Ortiz, and she recommended UV-filtering acrylic with a five-centimeter ventilation gap behind the glass, rather than ordinary glass mounted directly against it. This is specifically to protect the stained glass from UV damage and to allow proper airflow, which prevents condensation and deterioration. I hadn't had a chance to bring this to the group yet, but I think it should factor into our plans.
